court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: The respondent filed H.M.O.P.No.68 of 1996 seeking divorce against the appellant. The divorce was granted by ex parte decree dated 06.02.1997. The appellant then filed O.S.No.45 of 1997 seeking maintenance for herself and her son, which was allowed with a sum of Rs.1,000/- per month for the appellant and Rs.500/- to minor son towards maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: The court can modify permanent alimony ordered by the trial court if there is a change in circumstances.
legal_principles.held: This Court thought it fit to invoke Section 25(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, by which this Court can modify the permanent alimony ordered by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: Once a decree of divorce is granted, the relationship of husband and wife ceases, and the appellant is not entitled to maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The learned First Appellate Judge has rightly held that compensation can be awarded under Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act only during subsistence of marriage. Once decree of divorce is granted, relationship of husband and wife ceases and appellant is not entitled to maintenance under Section 25(2) of Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: The fair and decreetal order dated 14.08.2015 made in C.M.A.No.2 of 2014 is confirmed, reversing the Judgment and Decree passed in H.M.O.P.No.26 of 2012 on the file of the Sub Court, Mannargudi dated 12.09.2013.
